documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of EGM
Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018

analysis.summary: SK Minerals & Additives Limited reported revenue of Rs. 318 crores for FY26, representing a 50% growth over FY25. The company has an executable order book of Rs. 55 crores, of which Rs. 42 crores is from government contracts.

guidance.claim: SK Minerals & Additives aims to scale its manufacturing contribution to 50% of total turnover in the next two to three years.
guidance.quote: Currently, 23% of our revenue comes from the manufacturing capabilities, but in the next two to three years, we want to scale the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50%, with overall increase in turnover also.

demand_outlook.claim: The company is focusing its flame-retardant products on the cable, wire, and electrical and electronics equipment industries.
demand_outlook.quote: This flame-retardant is being used in various industries, but currently, we are focusing on cable and wire and electrical and electronics equipment.

demand_outlook.claim: Management plans to target EV batteries after catering to the cable, wire, and electronics segments.
demand_outlook.quote: Once we cater to these two segments, then we will target EV batteries also.

capex_expansion.claim: SK Minerals & Additives plans to scale total capacity from 600 metric tons to 18,000 metric tons in phases over the next 12 to 18 months.
capex_expansion.quote: So, from the current capacity of 600 metric ton, we will take it to 18,000 metric ton in phase manner of next 12 to 18 months.

capex_expansion.claim: The company acquired 9.6 acres of land for developing its polymer additives and polymer compound facility.
capex_expansion.quote: First of all, this 9.6 acre land which we have taken is for developing our polymer additives and polymer compound facility, whereas specified that in next 12 to 18 months, we will be taking our manufacturing capabilities to 18,000 metric tons.

margins_costs.claim: In FY26, EBITDA margins increased from 9% to 10% and PAT margins increased from 5% to 6%.
margins_costs.quote: Our financial performance, which is last financial year we have closed is Rs. 318 crores we have closed and this is 50% growth from the Financial Year ‘25 and our EBITDA margins have increased from 9% to 10% and PAT has increased from 5% to 6%.

margins_costs.claim: Margin contraction in H2 FY26 was caused by increased raw material prices.
margins_costs.quote: It is because of the increase in the prices of raw materials.

margins_costs.claim: Manufacturing margins stand at approximately 30%, whereas polymer additives margins are anticipated to be 40%.
margins_costs.quote: Currently, in terms of the manufacturing margins, we are standing at 30% approximately, whereas from polymer additives, we feel that the margins would be 40%.

orders_capacity.claim: The company maintains an order book of approximately Rs. 55 crores.
orders_capacity.quote: Currently, order book is around about Rs. 55 crore and it depends upon the customer.

orders_capacity.claim: Government clients account for Rs. 42 crores of the total Rs. 55 crore order book.
orders_capacity.quote: Out of these Rs. 55 crores, Rs. 42 crores is from government and rest is from private.

orders_capacity.claim: The company's current total installed capacity is 6,600 metric tons.
orders_capacity.quote: The current capacity is 6600 metric tons.

orders_capacity.claim: Capacity utilization for the food and feed segment is currently at 95%.
orders_capacity.quote: Food and feed is being running at 95%, and the polymer additive industry is yet to get live in the next three months.

capital_allocation.claim: The company's working capital cycle stands at 110 days.
capital_allocation.quote: Currently, working capital cycle is of 110 days.

capital_allocation.claim: The expansion to 18,000 metric tons capacity will be funded via bank credit lines and IPO proceeds.
capital_allocation.quote: We have the credit lines available for CAPEX from the banks also. And we have some part of the IPO proceeds which we have raised for CAPEX. So, we will utilize both for taking our capacity to next level to 18,000 metric tons.

risks_headwinds.claim: The newly established 400 metric tons per month polymer additives plant is experiencing teething issues.
risks_headwinds.quote: In terms of polymer additives, we have recently set up 400 metric ton plant per month, but there are some teething problems going on which we will try to address in the next three months and that will be also utilized fully in the next six months’ timeline.

risks_headwinds.claim: Geopolitical conditions have affected import trading inventory, causing stock to dry up.
risks_headwinds.quote: In terms of the import trading, yes, it has impacted because we have three months’ stock always available with us. So, that stock is getting dried up.

management_commitments.claim: The company plans a CAPEX of Rs. 20 crores over the next two years.
management_commitments.quote: Basically, we are looking at a CAPEX of Rs. 20 crores in the next two years.

management_commitments.claim: Management aims to scale manufacturing contribution to 50% of turnover in the next two to three years.
management_commitments.quote: Currently, 23% of our revenue comes from the manufacturing capabilities, but in the next two to three years, we want to scale the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50%, with overall increase in turnover also.

management_commitments.claim: The company aims to address teething issues at the polymer additives plant within the next three months.
management_commitments.quote: In terms of polymer additives, we have recently set up 400 metric ton plant per month, but there are some teething problems going on which we will try to address in the next three months and that will be also utilized fully in the next six months’ timeline.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
